summary.reviewGroupsNote: 35 active lesson groups, 73 question groups, 58 formula cards and 375 glossary entries; overlapping review groups, not a count of independent atomic facts.

corrections: Moved cumulative RISC/CISC questions after encoding prerequisites; added local instruction-boundary, popcount and narrow argument-width teaching for existing exercises.
A five-bit register field counts 32 encodings, including an instruction-specific special pattern, not 32 general-purpose registers.
Explicitly distinguish sixteen-byte x86 recursive frames from thirty-two-byte A64 frames in the displayed listings.
Load/store descriptions permit specialised atomics; fixed-width left shifts can discard high bits; three-operand source preservation assumes distinct destination.
Broaden PC-relative reference-point explanation to distinguish current A64 PC from next x86 RIP.
GOT slots need not remain writable after full RELRO; lazy binding does not eliminate every unused-function startup cost.

C memory and linking definitions now distinguish ordinary versus exceptional cases: signed/unsigned overflow, ELF segments versus metadata, static archive order, strong/weak references and runtime resource dependencies.
Canaries detect changed guards when checked; a crossing overwrite need not always change the guard. General code reuse and out-of-bounds reads no longer open overly narrow ROP/write-only definitions.

BTI includes compatible PAC landing instructions, and CET/PAC claims require applicable enabled features. Removed an unsupported fixed branch-misprediction penalty and universal linker speed/deprecation claims.

gaps: No original lesson, question or substantive example removed: all 12 archives and all 43 original code/diagram/trace bodies preserved.
Advanced SIMD/SVE/SME ABI variations, every linker/OS extension, physical x86 timing and concurrent self-modifying-code correctness remain outside this scalar introductory scope.
